title: Siberian Dawn / Gulag Landscape
placement: Used once, with extreme care, in the Stalinist Terror or Gulag thematic essay (small treatment recommended)
purpose: The scale of the system and the emptiness of the place where people disappeared.
prompt: Powerful, restrained documentary-style image for the Soviet section of a serious history site. Immense, empty Siberian landscape at first light — endless taiga and low hills, a single distant wooden watchtower from a Gulag camp barely visible on the horizon, heavy snow, pale pink and steel blue sky. Conveys scale, isolation, and historical gravity without any human figures or sensationalism.
altText: Vast empty Siberian landscape at dawn with a single distant Gulag watchtower on the horizon.
extendedDescription: One of the most restrained and powerful images in the collection. The focus is on the crushing scale of the landscape and the tiny, almost invisible human structure in the distance. No figures. No barbed wire close-ups. Pure geography and implication. This image must be used with extreme sensitivity and only in the most serious thematic contexts.
notes: HIGHEST SENSITIVITY. Requires explicit historian sign-off before any public use. Consider smaller size or making it optional/expandable.
